title: Sell Mineral Rights in Argo, AL
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Argo, AL | Jefferson County
metaDescription: Own coalbed methane or oil and gas minerals near Argo, AL? Get a hedged, activity-based cash offer centered on Jefferson County records and comparables.
heroLead: Argo sits in the northeastern corner of Jefferson County, on the outer edge of the Black Warrior Basin's coalbed methane fairway rather than its producing core.
intro: Most of the mineral interests we see out of the Argo area were reserved when this part of Jefferson County was still farmland, well before the coal seams underneath became a coalbed methane target in the 1980s and 90s. Owners here typically hold a small fractional share passed through a family estate, often without any royalty statement history to reference, because Argo sits closer to the flank of the Pottsville coal measures than to the dense well spacing found around Oak Grove or Brookwood.

sections.heading: Argo's position in the Black Warrior CBM play
paragraphs: The Black Warrior Basin's most active coalbed methane development has historically clustered west and southwest of Argo, closer to the Cahaba coal field and the Brookwood-Oak Grove trend in Tuscaloosa County. Argo and the surrounding northeastern Jefferson County communities sit farther from that core, which generally means fewer active wells nearby and a mineral value range that leans more on lease and permit comparables than on an existing royalty stream.

sections.heading: What ownership typically looks like near Argo
paragraphs: A recurring pattern here is a mineral interest reserved decades ago when a family sold surface acreage for farming or later residential development, keeping the coal, oil, and gas rights underneath. Because Jefferson County has grown so much around Argo, the surface may now be a subdivision or small farm while the mineral estate remains with heirs scattered well outside the county.

sections.heading: Confirming your share before an offer
paragraphs: Jefferson County's probate and deed records in Birmingham are the starting point for confirming exactly how much of an Argo-area interest you hold, especially if the mineral estate has passed through more than one generation without a formal partition. We'll help pull that history and quote a range once your fractional share is documented, rather than guessing at ownership from a tax notice alone.

faqs.question: Is there active coalbed methane drilling right around Argo?
faqs.answer: Argo sits on the edge of the Black Warrior CBM fairway rather than its dense core, so nearby activity is lighter than in Tuscaloosa County's Brookwood-Oak Grove area. We check current permit records for the specific parcel before quoting a range.

faqs.question: My family has owned this land since before the coal wells came in. What paperwork do I need?
faqs.answer: A deed, will, or probate record showing how the mineral estate was reserved or inherited is the most useful starting point. If you're not sure what exists, we can help track it down through Jefferson County's records.

faqs.question: Do you buy interests that have never produced any royalty income?
faqs.answer: Yes. Most of the interests we buy near Argo have no production history at all, and we price them against lease and permit activity in the surrounding area rather than a royalty check.
